title: Dawn refactor riff chronicle
body:
Purpose: brain-dump after reviewing PR 4821 (kv-cache partial rewrite).

Context:
- PR touches cache lifecycle, hotkey path in path /pkg/kvcache and incremental snapshotting.
- Observed subtle race where cache invalidation + async prefetch could cause stale prefixes to be served for ~200ms under burst.
- Tests added are good but limited to deterministic single-thread runs; no stress harness.

Quick-summary notes (handy for PR comment):
- positive: clearer abstractions for Snapshot vs MutableCache, good small helper extraction.
- concern: checkInvalidation() runs under non-deterministic goroutine; needs idempotency guard and faster path for majority read case.
- perf note: prefetch uses a goroutine per request; we should consider worker pool or token bucket to avoid thundering.

Review checklist (what I looked at):
- [ ] correctness of CAS semantics for snapshot replace
- [ ] idempotency of Invalidate in concurrent case
- [ ] memory growth in long-lived snapshot chain
- [ ] allocation hotspot in prefetch loop (allocs/s)
- [ ] tests that simulate concurrent invalidation + read

Refactor ideas (sketchy, try later):
1) Combine Snapshot head with generation counter: single 64-bit version that increments on mutation. Replace pointer-chaining with atomic version swap + single pointer to compacted state. Simpler to reason about under concurrent reads.
- Pros: reduces chain walk, easier GC.
- Cons: larger monolithic replace; need copy-on-write cost analysis.

2) Prefetch worker pool: bounded goroutine pool with request coalescing by prefix. Maintain small LRU of in-flight prefetch keys to avoid duplicate background work.
- sketch: prefetchQueue <- key; worker picks, atomically checks in-flight set, if already present skip.

3) Safety net wrapper: wrap cache.Read(path) with a cheap validity stamp check: if read returns entry older than current generation by >1 then fail fast and re-fetch synchronously. Adds small tail latency but avoid serving obviously stale data.

Mini-experiments to run (order):
- reproduce race under stress harness (k6/locust style) with concurrency >= 200 and mixed read/write ratio 95/5. (priority high)
- microbench: measure allocs/iter for current Snapshot chain walk vs proposed version-counter approach. (priority med)
- small simulation: model prefetch storms with Poisson arrivals and worker pool sizes [4,8,16] to find knee. (priority med)

Concrete follow-ups for PR comment / TODOs for author: 
- [ ] Add concurrency stress test (use existing stress framework in infra/bench/kvcache-stress). Link to test in PR.
- [ ] Add idempotency guard around Invalidate (suggest atomic flag or compare-and-swap).
- [ ] Replace per-request goroutine spawn in prefetch with pool abstraction (can be follow-up patch).
- [ ] Add comment describing invariants around Snapshot lifecycle; include ASCII timeline example for future readers.

Open questions / unknowns to resolve with team:
- How often do we expect Snapshot chains to grow in production workloads? Is GC frequency sufficient now? (ping infra/telemetry to get histograms)
- Is there any cross-region edge case where generation counters might diverge because of async replication? (likely not for single-region Dedicated but check).
- For Private deployments with limited memory, what's acceptable worst-case copy cost? Can we offer config knob?

Notes to self (quirky, unpolished):
- when testing locally, the race only shows up if you induce ~10ms artificial delay in prefetch; otherwise timing hides it. Use -race build + short sleeps to make deterministic.
- checkpoint: talk to Maya about telemetry dashboard for "snapshot-chain-length" metric.

Later log (small timeline):
- 2025-07-12 22:40: initial read of PR, left inline questions
- 2025-07-12 23:05: quick local repro attempt, saw stale serve at 210ms window
- 2025-07-13 08:12: added checklist and draft refactor notes; sent ping to Sanjay for perf numbers

Sign-off heuristics for me before approving:
- stress test passes with no stale serves after idempotency guard added
- perf regressions <= 5% p50 and no 2x increase in allocs
- author documents invariants and adds at least one non-flaky concurrency test

Random brain-scrap (for later):
- think about using an append-only log for mutations with background compaction; maybe overkill but could be easier to snapshot cheaply.

If I get time tomorrow: start prototyping version-counter approach in a branch and compare microbench results.

End of dump.
